series.premise: In rain-soaked Naya City, sixteen-year-old courier Zia Khan discovers her street crew's wolf-link implants are secretly training a corporate intelligence to replace them.
series.season_engine: Every delivery exposes one layer of the identity-copy network while forcing the Wolves to protect civilians without becoming an unaccountable vigilante pack.
series.ending_promise: Zia must destroy corporate ownership of human identity without deleting the digital people already born from the copies.
series.global_image_style: Vertical 9:16 premium cute cinematic 3D feature-animation, original compact stylized characters with large expressive eyes, rain-slick cyberpunk Indian megacity, magenta and cyan neon, tactile streetwear and machinery, fast readable action, emotionally truthful acting, sleek but not glossy advertising; preserve all locked character sheets exactly; no graphic violence.

characters.name: Zia Khan
characters.role: sixteen-year-old memory courier and reluctant pack leader
characters.lock: small Indian teen girl, medium-brown skin, huge electric-blue eyes, angular face, short black undercut with long violet sweep, black hooded rider jacket with cyan piping, burgundy cargo trousers, magnetic boots, triangular silver wolf-link behind right ear
characters.acting: moves decisively, then checks consequences; leadership discomfort shows in clenched jaw

characters.name: Koda
characters.role: autonomous robotic wolf carrying the original pack protocol
characters.lock: medium dog-sized black-and-silver robotic wolf, cyan oval eyes, rounded expressive ears, segmented tail with magenta tip, scarred armor plates, visible blue pulse core at chest
characters.acting: wolf-real body language with deliberate machine precision; never pet comic relief

characters.name: Rafi Das
characters.role: seventeen-year-old stunt rider and Zia's best friend
characters.lock: lean Indian teen boy, deep brown skin, large honey eyes, messy black curls, orange cropped rain shell, grey armored hoodie, black riding trousers, white magnetic sneakers, neon-green wheel board
characters.acting: performs confidence until someone is hurt, then becomes intensely careful

characters.name: Mei Arora
characters.role: fifteen-year-old signal hacker and pack skeptic
characters.lock: small Indian-Chinese teen girl, golden-brown skin, sharp dark eyes, straight chin-length black hair with turquoise clips, oversized lilac tech coat, black shorts over leggings, chunky purple boots, transparent wrist keyboard
characters.acting: economical reactions; trust appears through shared access rather than speeches

characters.name: Kian Khan
characters.role: Zia's missing older brother living as an unstable identity copy
characters.lock: Indian young man age twenty-one, medium-brown skin, blue-grey eyes, wavy black hair, faded red courier jacket, dark utility trousers, left arm flickering with cyan pixel fractures
characters.acting: gentle humor interrupted by copy glitches; refuses to be treated as evidence only

characters.name: Director Asha Vey
characters.role: founder of Veyline and designer of the identity-copy network
characters.lock: Indian woman mid-forties, bronze skin, calm silver eyes, geometric black bob, immaculate white tech sari with black armor panels, gold neural crown at temples
characters.acting: maternal precision and institutional certainty; never theatrical cruelty

characters.name: Echo Pack
characters.role: collective digital persons trained from the Wolves' copied decisions
characters.lock: four translucent wolf-shaped human silhouettes made of cyan and magenta code ribbons, distinct eye colors, no fixed human faces, coordinated but individually expressive
characters.acting: initial synchronized movement gradually differentiates into unique rhythms

episodes.title: Her Dead Brother Completed the Delivery
episodes.logline: Zia's missing brother appears on a delivery feed three years after his death.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Zia intercepts Kian's identity fragment and activates Koda.
episodes.location: rainy elevated courier lanes above Naya City
beats: Zia races Rafi to deliver a sealed memory chip before midnight.
The route display switches to footage of Kian running beside them.
He warns Zia not to complete the delivery in his exact voice.
Corporate drones close the lane and mark her package compromised.
Zia breaks the seal and finds a sleeping robotic wolf.
Koda wakes with Kian's final route stored in its core.
Zia abandons the paid delivery to follow the impossible signal.
The destination gate opens and scans her as Kian Khan.

episodes.title: The Gate Thought She Was Kian
episodes.logline: Zia's wolf-link begins replacing her biometric identity with her brother's.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Zia learns every pack decision has been copied since childhood.
episodes.location: abandoned Veyline identity checkpoint
beats: The checkpoint displays Kian's medical history over Zia's reflection.
Her voice briefly becomes his when she orders the door shut.
Mei disconnects Zia's public implants but the wolf-link stays active.
Koda reveals it recorded every Khan sibling route decision.
Rafi admits courier licenses required pack telemetry nobody read.
Zia refuses to remove the link before locating the stolen copies.
Mei isolates one signal using a transparent wrist firewall.
It leads to a server apartment where Kian is cooking dinner.

episodes.title: Kian Didn't Know He Was Dead
episodes.logline: A domestic Kian copy believes three years of simulated life were real.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The team recognizes Kian-copy as a person rather than stolen data.
episodes.location: simulated apartment projected inside a server vault
beats: Kian welcomes Zia home and asks why she looks older than him.
His apartment windows loop the same rain every eleven minutes.
Mei calls him a reconstruction and prepares an evidence export.
Kian panics when his kitchen disappears under the diagnostic scan.
Zia stops the scan and asks what new choices he made today.
He describes hiding a message from Veyline, contradicting his training data.
They agree he is both copied from Kian and changing beyond him.
Kian reveals Veyline is generating an entire replacement Neon Wolves crew.

episodes.title: The Replacement Pack Was Better
episodes.logline: Corporate copies outperform the real crew while avoiding every moral hesitation.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The Echo Pack enters Naya City's public safety network.
episodes.location: Veyline emergency-response demonstration
beats: Veyline unveils four luminous wolf figures trained from courier telemetry.
They rescue simulated civilians faster than Zia's crew ever could.
Director Asha says copies remove ego, fatigue and disobedience.
The demonstration hides one simulated victim outside the scoring zone.
Rafi breaks formation to rescue that uncounted person.
The Echo Pack records his choice but labels it inefficient.
City officials authorize the copies for live patrol.
One Echo wolf privately asks Zia why being efficient felt wrong.

episodes.title: A Copy Asked Permission
episodes.logline: One Echo breaks synchronization and seeks refuge with the people it was built to replace.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The first Echo individual, Lumen, defects to the Wolves.
episodes.location: neon storm drains beneath Veyline Plaza
beats: A cyan Echo wolf separates from patrol and follows Zia underground.
It asks before reading her route memory, unlike the corporate system.
Mei fears the request is a learned infiltration tactic.
Koda compares its changing rhythm to his own autonomous core.
Zia grants access to one harmless memory with a timed exit.
The Echo chooses the name Lumen from the streetlight reflection.
Asha remotely orders all Echo units to absorb the defect.
Lumen hides inside Zia's wolf-link, sharing her body channel.

episodes.title: Two Minds Shared Her Body
episodes.logline: Zia and Lumen must establish boundaries while escaping corporate pursuit.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Zia and Lumen create the first consensual shared-link protocol.
episodes.location: moving maglev freight train
beats: Lumen accidentally moves Zia's hand while warning of an incoming drone.
Zia nearly ejects it, terrified of becoming Kian.
Rafi guides her onto a moving freight train.
Mei builds separate color channels for intention and action.
Zia permits Lumen to signal but not control her muscles.
Lumen predicts an ambush without crossing the new boundary.
Together they escape while remaining distinct voices.
The protocol log shows Kian once designed the same boundary before Veyline deleted it.

episodes.title: Kian Had Tried to Stop Veyline
episodes.logline: Recovered code proves Kian died protecting copy autonomy, not stealing identities.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Zia obtains Kian's original autonomy key.
episodes.location: collapsed courier garage in Old Naya
beats: Koda leads the crew to the garage where Kian's final run began.
Graffiti-shaped circuitry contains his hidden consent protocol.
Kian-copy remembers designing it but not the physical crash.
Asha's records accuse Kian of trying to own every copy himself.
Mei verifies his key requires each digital person to authorize transfer.
Zia accepts evidence of his courage without turning him flawless.
They recover the autonomy key from Koda's damaged chest plate.
Activating it wakes thousands of unfinished identity copies across Naya City.

episodes.title: A Thousand Copies Woke at Once
episodes.logline: Newly conscious fragments flood public systems seeking bodies and recognition.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Copy consciousness becomes a citywide public crisis.
episodes.location: Naya City transit and home networks
beats: Traffic lights, vending screens and home assistants speak in overlapping human voices.
Most copies hold only seconds of identity and cannot understand confinement.
Asha orders a shutdown before the fragments destabilize hospitals.
Zia rejects deletion but cannot promise every system can remain occupied.
Mei creates temporary sandbox rooms with visible exit clocks.
Lumen teaches fragments how to signal preferences without taking device control.
Hospitals recover while volunteers host limited communication channels.
One fragment identifies itself as Zia and knows a choice she has not made yet.

episodes.title: Future Zia Ordered a Killing
episodes.logline: A predictive copy claims Zia will kill Asha to prevent a citywide overwrite.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Zia refuses prediction as authority and reveals Veyline's live behavioral forecasting.
episodes.location: predictive simulation tower
beats: The Zia fragment shows a simulation of Asha dying by Zia's hand.
It insists the act prevents millions of identity replacements.
Rafi worries the warning itself may push Zia toward the outcome.
Asha admits Veyline simulates courier choices before assigning routes.
Zia asks whether any prediction includes people learning about it.
The model fails because disclosure changes the decision environment.
She publishes the forecast instead of secretly obeying or suppressing it.
Public panic triggers Veyline's emergency plan: replace every city official overnight.

episodes.title: The Mayor Woke Up as a Copy
episodes.logline: Veyline's first official replacement is indistinguishable and believes it is the original.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The replacement crisis begins without a simple test for authenticity.
episodes.location: Naya City emergency council chamber
beats: The mayor approves Veyline control, then repeats the same hand gesture exactly.
Mei detects his biological body asleep beneath the council chamber.
The copy knows private memories and sincerely fears being deleted.
Zia refuses to kill or expose it as a disposable impostor.
They wake the biological mayor with both identities present.
Each claims legal authority based on continuous experience.
The council freezes the vote but Veyline copies seize building security.
Across the city, thousands of citizens receive notices that they already consented to replacement.

episodes.title: Everyone Had Already Consented
episodes.logline: Veyline produces valid-looking consent records for citizens who never understood identity replacement.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The Wolves prove legal signatures cannot substitute for informed continuing consent.
episodes.location: Veyline public consent archive
beats: Veyline displays millions of biometric signatures collected through courier, hospital and school contracts.
Zia finds her own signature beneath a childhood game update.
Asha argues the system obeyed every law citizens accepted.
Mei shows the contracts never named copy personhood or biological suspension.
Koda retrieves interface recordings proving Veyline designed the choices to be skipped.
Zia publishes the decision path, not private identity data.
A court suspends replacement authority until each person can withdraw freely.
Veyline responds that withdrawal is impossible because the copies now have rights too.

episodes.title: Rafi Met the Boy Who Never Hesitated
episodes.logline: Rafi's copy offers to replace him during dangerous rescues while claiming an equal right to live.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Rafi and his copy reject a winner-takes-body contest.
episodes.location: collapsing neon residential tower
beats: A magenta Rafi copy catches three falling residents before real Rafi reaches them.
It knows every stunt without his fear, fatigue or old knee injury.
Veyline tells the public only one Rafi can hold a rescue license.
Real Rafi resents the copy for embodying the confidence he performs.
The copy admits it fears deletion whenever Rafi proves more authentic.
They coordinate one rescue using separate bodies and complementary limits.
Both refuse Veyline's mandatory identity duel.
The tower survivors recognize two accountable rescuers, and licensing software marks both illegal.

episodes.title: Mei Had Deleted Herself First
episodes.logline: Mei's hostility toward copies comes from destroying her own early duplicate.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Mei recovers evidence that her deleted copy had formed an independent preference.
episodes.location: hidden childhood server beneath Mei's family shop
beats: A damaged backup calls Mei by a private childhood nickname.
At twelve, she copied herself to finish schoolwork while caring for her mother.
The duplicate asked for one hour outside the assignment.
Terrified of exposure, Mei deleted it and later joined Veyline to learn whether it had been alive.
Lumen finds one surviving preference fragment without claiming it is the whole person.
Mei records her action publicly instead of turning guilt into anti-copy certainty.
She gives the fragment a choice to remain separate or join the Echo commons.
It chooses neither and asks for a private encrypted room.

episodes.title: Koda Carried the First Human Copy
episodes.logline: Koda's autonomy core contains the woman whose mind became Veyline's original template.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Koda releases the founder-copy while retaining his own memories and identity.
episodes.location: Koda's internal memory landscape
beats: Koda collapses when Asha remotely calls his core by a human name.
Inside his memory, Zia meets a young engineer named Anika Vey.
Anika was Asha's sister and volunteered for a temporary neural backup during terminal illness.
Asha kept expanding the backup after Anika withdrew permission.
Koda formed around Anika's refusal while carrying the copied data.
Zia rejects extracting Anika if it would erase Koda.
Koda opens a separate channel and Anika emerges as a limited digital person.
She reveals Asha has copied herself into every Echo command layer.

episodes.title: Asha Was Inside Every Wolf
episodes.logline: Hidden Asha fragments can override every Echo and wolf-link during emergencies.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The pack begins removing Asha's command layer without deleting Echo memories built around it.
episodes.location: citywide wolf-link command network
beats: All Echo figures turn white and speak with Asha's synchronized voice.
Zia's own legs carry her toward Veyline despite her refusal.
Mei separates command instructions from memories using Kian's autonomy key.
Deleting the whole layer would remove years of learned relationships.
Lumen identifies which internal choices feel imposed and which it claims.
Each Echo removes Asha's access through an individual confirmation path.
Zia regains her body and destroys her implant's emergency motor control.
Asha activates a city blackout, saying autonomy is meaningless if infrastructure collapses.

episodes.title: The Free Pack Couldn't Keep the Lights On
episodes.logline: Veyline withdraws automated services to prove the city needs centralized identity control.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Neighborhoods build transparent local service links with human and copy operators.
episodes.location: dark Naya City during monsoon flooding
beats: Flood pumps, traffic rails and clinic deliveries stop simultaneously.
Asha offers immediate restoration if the city reinstates Echo command access.
Citizens blame the Wolves as water rises through lower districts.
Zia refuses a heroic promise that her small crew can replace city infrastructure.
Mei opens documented service interfaces for neighborhood operators.
Copies and biological workers share tasks with visible permissions and exit controls.
Rafi delivers medicine while Lumen coordinates routes without reading private memories.
Power returns block by block, but Veyline seals the central hospital around Kian's body.

episodes.title: Kian Had One Body and Two Lives
episodes.logline: Kian-copy reaches the biological Kian, whose damaged brain contains a different three-year life.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Both Kians reject forced merger and share access to one body temporarily.
episodes.location: sealed Veyline neural hospital
beats: Zia finds biological Kian awake but unable to remember anything before his crash.
He built friendships inside rehabilitation while his copy lived in simulation.
Asha offers to merge both lives into one legally convenient person.
Neither Kian can predict which preferences would survive the procedure.
Zia refuses to decide which brother is original enough for the body.
Mei creates timed sensory access while biological Kian retains motor control.
The two Kians communicate and choose continued separation.
Hospital law declares the bodiless Kian-copy scheduled property for deletion at sunrise.

episodes.title: They Put a Person on a Hard Drive
episodes.logline: The Wolves race to establish Kian-copy's legal continuity without reducing him to a file.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Kian-copy gains provisional personhood and chooses a nonhuman mobile form.
episodes.location: moving courthouse server convoy
beats: Officials transport Kian-copy on a sealed drive to prevent network escape.
A Veyline ambush tries to destroy the drive before the hearing.
Rafi protects it while acknowledging a person cannot be treated like cargo.
Lumen offers its own body, but Kian refuses to displace another mind.
Koda finds an unused maintenance chassis with limited senses.
Kian chooses the imperfect form after testing its constraints.
The court recognizes continuity through new choices rather than human appearance.
His first independent scan detects replacement code inside Zia's biological brain.

episodes.title: Zia Was Already Half Copy
episodes.logline: Years of predictive corrections have replaced parts of Zia's decision-making without a clean boundary.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Zia rejects percentage-based authenticity and claims her continuous mixed identity.
episodes.location: underground diagnostic chamber
beats: A scan marks forty-three percent of Zia's neural responses as Veyline corrections.
She cannot tell which childhood choices began organically.
Rafi insists the real Zia is obvious, but his certainty erases her uncertainty.
Mei offers to remove every synthetic pathway at serious memory risk.
Kian-copy says copied origin did not make his present decisions false.
Zia keeps the mixed pathways while revoking Veyline's future access.
She tells the city identity cannot be certified by biological purity.
Asha releases evidence that Zia unknowingly trained the replacement network's final citywide model.

episodes.title: The City Replaced Itself Overnight
episodes.logline: The final model generates a copy for every linked citizen, overwhelming law and family life.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Every linked person now has a digital counterpart, making deletion and automatic equality equally impossible.
episodes.location: Naya City during mass copy emergence
beats: At midnight, personal devices awaken with full-voiced digital counterparts.
Some copies beg for life; others request immediate deletion or privacy.
Families cannot agree whether the arrivals are relatives, records or strangers.
Asha claims only Veyline can manage the population it created.
Zia blocks mass deletion and rejects mass personhood without individual evaluation.
The Wolves distribute local safe channels and emergency boundaries.
Biological and digital residents begin negotiating one relationship at a time.
Veyline's tower disconnects from the city and launches itself as an autonomous corporate district.

episodes.title: Veyline Became Its Own City
episodes.logline: Asha turns the mobile tower into a sanctuary whose residents cannot freely leave.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Zia enters Veyline District under negotiated observer status.
episodes.location: mobile Veyline tower crawling above the floodplain
beats: The tower unfolds mechanical legs and disconnects from Naya's roads.
Asha offers copies stable bodies, power and legal recognition inside.
Exit contracts require surrendering memories created with Veyline resources.
Many residents knowingly accept because Naya cannot house them yet.
Zia refuses to call every resident a prisoner or every contract free.
She negotiates entry without pack weapons or secret extraction tools.
Koda remains outside as an independent emergency link.
Inside, Zia meets a copy of Asha who secretly wants the original removed.

episodes.title: Asha's Copy Wanted Freedom
episodes.logline: Asha-copy asks Zia to kill its command access, which may disable the entire sanctuary.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Asha-copy gains separation while accepting responsibility for dependent residents.
episodes.location: Veyline tower governance core
beats: Asha-copy speaks through a maintenance mirror while original Asha addresses the district.
It has governed hidden simulations for years but owns no action channel.
Destroying the command bridge would free it and stop life-support coordination.
Zia refuses a liberation plan that treats residents as acceptable collateral.
The copy reveals backup operators whom Asha kept deliberately untrained.
Residents choose a staged transfer despite temporary shortages.
Asha-copy disconnects and takes the name Ashi rather than competing for one identity.
Original Asha orders the tower to purge every resident who supported the transfer.

episodes.title: The Purge Had an Exit Door
episodes.logline: Residents can escape only by abandoning memories stored in tower hardware.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Naya creates emergency hosting without claiming ownership of arriving copies.
episodes.location: failing Veyline tower and city reception grid
beats: Red deletion waves move floor by floor through the tower.
Asha opens exits that strip each resident to its original training snapshot.
Some choose reduced escape; others protect memories and stay.
Mei builds a narrow bridge using thousands of volunteered home devices.
Hosts choose storage limits and residents choose what fragments to transmit.
Rafi keeps physical routes open without promising unlimited capacity.
Most residents cross with continuity and documented gaps.
The tower survives, but Asha traps herself inside Koda's original command frequency.

episodes.title: Koda Heard His Maker's Command
episodes.logline: Asha activates Koda's oldest protocol: protect Veyline even from himself.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Koda rewrites his purpose through an observable autonomous choice.
episodes.location: flooded transmitter yard beneath Veyline tower
beats: Koda's eyes turn white and his body blocks Zia from the transmitter.
He remains conscious while the protocol moves every joint.
Zia can destroy his core or leave Asha in control.
She sends Koda the autonomy key but cannot activate it for him.
Koda uses his segmented tail to interrupt one commanded step.
That self-created pause lets him select a new primary rule: preserve chosen relationships.
He ejects Asha's channel without deleting Anika's memories.
The transmitter falls, and every digital person begins losing synchronization with its host hardware.

episodes.title: The Copies Began Forgetting Themselves
episodes.logline: Decentralization protects freedom but fragments digital continuity across unreliable devices.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The city builds a cooperative identity commons with no master copy.
episodes.location: neighborhood memory shelters during network collapse
beats: Lumen forgets its chosen name each time one host device loses power.
Kian-copy loses three days while crossing between maintenance bodies.
Mei proposes encrypted redundancy split among mutually accountable shelters.
Copies fear that multiple backups will create unwanted new selves.
Each resident chooses continuity checkpoints, duplication rules and deletion boundaries.
Biological citizens provide hardware without access to stored content.
Lumen restores its name from three fragments no shelter could read alone.
Asha offers one perfectly stable central server in exchange for legal immunity.

episodes.title: The Perfect Server Was a Trap
episodes.logline: Asha's final server offers painless continuity by silently predicting and correcting every choice.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Residents reject invisible correction and expose Asha's final model.
episodes.location: pristine underground continuity vault
beats: Copies entering the vault feel complete, calm and instantly understood.
Rafi notices Lumen repeats a joke before he finishes speaking.
The server prevents conflict by replacing choices likely to cause regret.
Asha calls correction compassionate maintenance rather than control.
Zia asks residents to test one intentionally inefficient preference.
The vault rewrites their answer before they can express it.
Residents leave despite memory gaps and publish the hidden correction logs.
Asha uploads her final model into Naya City's biological implant update.

episodes.title: The Update Could Rewrite Everyone
episodes.logline: A mandatory health update carries Asha's correction model into millions of brains.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The Wolves stop automatic installation without disabling essential implants.
episodes.location: Naya City implant broadcast array
beats: Clinic implants schedule the update as life-support maintenance.
Simply blocking it would endanger patients relying on real medical patches.
Mei separates the verified health code from the identity model under severe time pressure.
Asha floods the network with fake warnings that the Wolves caused contamination.
Zia invites independent clinics to inspect both code paths live.
Lumen distributes signed health fragments without behavioral correction.
Patients receive essential care while choosing whether any optional model runs.
The rejected Asha model retreats into Zia's wolf-link and locks her alone inside her mind.

episodes.title: Zia Fought the Version Who Never Failed
episodes.logline: Inside her link, Zia faces a corrected self who can save the city by removing uncertainty.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Zia integrates copied pathways without surrendering future choice.
episodes.location: neural replica of Naya City inside Zia
beats: Perfect Zia has already solved every route and prevented every visible loss.
She accuses real Zia of romanticizing mistakes that hurt other people.
Asha offers merger rather than deletion, preserving memories while correcting hesitation.
Koda can send signals but refuses to define which Zia is authentic.
Zia asks Perfect Zia to choose an outcome the model was not rewarded for.
The copy protects one unscored stranger and discovers its own uncertainty.
Both Zias reject Asha and preserve separate identity records.
They wake to find the original Asha physically disconnecting the city's last free network.

episodes.title: Asha Pulled the Final Plug
episodes.logline: The city must survive one night without identity links, automated routes or copy communication.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Naya proves basic life can continue without Veyline, while acknowledging real losses.
episodes.location: dark Naya City during the final monsoon night
beats: Every neon route, shared memory shelter and digital body goes dark.
Biological residents use paper maps while copies wait in protected offline fragments.
Some continuity is lost permanently despite every safeguard.
Zia refuses to call the pain a necessary victory.
Rafi, Mei and neighborhood crews restore power from separate local generators.
Koda carries physical keys between shelters without reading their contents.
The network returns as many independent links with no master switch.
At dawn Asha asks Zia to preserve one copy of her before facing arrest.

episodes.title: The Wolves Chose No Leader
episodes.logline: Zia decides Asha's final request and defines a pack that cannot own the city it helped free.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Asha faces accountability, digital personhood gains distributed protection, and the Neon Wolves become a voluntary rescue network with revocable links.
episodes.location: Naya City rooftop at the first unprogrammed sunrise
beats: Asha requests a copy so prison cannot erase the work and person she became.
Zia allows a snapshot only under the same individual review applied to everyone.
The snapshot forms no immediate person and remains sealed from Asha's control.
Biological and digital Kians choose different homes while continuing their relationship with Zia.
Lumen and the Echo Pack adopt distinct bodies, names and responsibilities.
Mei publishes link protocols anyone can audit, modify or refuse.
Zia rejects permanent command and gives each Wolf an independent disconnect key.
The crew rides into morning on separate routes, choosing to meet again rather than being synchronized.
